recipes.name: One-Pan Mongolian Beef Noodles with broccoli
ingredients: 4 instant noodle cakes (, ~70g/2.5oz each (aka 2 minute noodles, instant ramen noodles), UNCOOKED, (Note 1))
2 tablespoons dark soy sauce - NOT light soy sauce or all-purpose soy sauce
1/4 cup hoisin sauce (- if yours is not a dark brown colour, noodles may be bit paler)
2 tablespoons Mirin (, or Chinese cooking wine + 2 tsp sugar (Note 3))
1/4 teaspoon Chinese Five Spice Powder ((not critical if you don't have))
2 tablespoons oil (- anything plain flavoured (eg canola, vegetable, peanut))
5 cups broccoli florets, cut small (, not too big else they get in the way and won't cook through (Note 4 for other veg))
instructions: Please do not make this recipe. See important announcement in Recipe Summary above. Thank you! - Nagi x

Mix sauce ingredients in a bowl. Heat oil on high heat in a large deep pan. Cook onion and garlic 30 sec, then cook beef. Stir in sauce, then stir in broccoli. Add water, bring to simmer, break noodles cakes in half and squidgy in. Leave 30 sec, turn, leave 30 sec, then toss 2 - 3 minutes until noodles are soft and all sauce is absorbed. Serve!
Sauce - Mix the ingredients in a small bowl.

Cook beef - Heat the oil in a large, deep 30cm / 12" pan over high heat (or use a large pot). Add the garlic and onion, cook for 30 seconds. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up as you go, until you no longer see red. Add the sauce and cook until the sauce has coated all the beef well.
Add the broccoli and stir it through to coat I sauce. No need to give it cooking time, I promise it cooks through in the next step!

Noodles - Add the water. When it starts bubbling, push the noodles in (break in half along direction of noodles so they fit more easily). Leave for 30 seconds, then turn the noodles. Leave another 30 seconds, then start tossing the noodles with two spatulas or tongs until the noodles are softened and there's no sauce left in the pan (2 - 3 minutes). If the noodles need a little longer, just add a bit more water.
Serve - Divide between bowls and enjoy! A drizzle of sriracha for some heat wouldn't go astray here. :)

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Instant noodle cakes – Also known as “2 minute noodles”, and ramen noodle cakes (common in the US). I buy plain in sleeves of 10, if yours comes with the seasoning packet, discard it, we only need the noodles, 2. Dark soy sauce has a strong soy flavour but is not as salty as light soy sauce. This is key to getting enough flavour in both the beef and noodles with the method of cooking used in this recipe so unfortunately it can’t be substituted with light soy sauce or all-purpose soy sauce. 3. Mirin – Sweet Japanese cooking rice wine that adds depth of flavour in an otherwise simple sauce! Sold at regular grocery stores these days. For alcohol free, replace half the water with chicken stock to make up for some of the lost flavour. 4. Other vegetables – carrot, cauliflower, capsicum, mushroom, green beans, baby corn or other vegetables that can hold up to 3 – 4 minutes in the pan will work just fine here. Leftovers will keep for 3 days in the fridge. I haven’t tried freezing but I see no reason why it wouldn’t work. Nutrition per serving, assuming 4 servings.
